strengths: Clear and well-motivated problem formulation with elegant mathematical treatment of synthesis routes as trees
Well-designed custom genetic operators (Grow, Shrink, Rerun, Change Internal, Change Leaf) that maintain synthesizability by construction

Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple diverse benchmarks (analog search, PMO with 22 tasks, docking), demonstrating SOTA performance on PMO (16.426 vs 16.304 for GPBO) and strong docking results
Thoughtful ML integration through building block filtering: simple classification for analog search and interpretable Neural Additive Models for property optimization
Solid reproducibility practices with detailed hyperparameters, promised code release, and extensive ablation studies (Tables 1, 6-9)
Always produces valid synthesis routes by design, unlike some baselines which generate invalid routes
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty: the core contribution is straightforward application of classical GA to synthesis tree representation; genetic operators are intuitive tree adaptations rather than novel algorithmic concepts

Significant computational efficiency disadvantage: 3× slower than SynFormer baseline (250m vs 80m), which is a serious practical limitation for adoption as standalone tool despite justification that search-based methods are inherently slower

Restrictive search space undermines standalone value: SynGA alone underperforms synthesis-agnostic methods on PMO (13.366 vs 16.304 for GPBO); requires expensive SynGBO wrapper to achieve SOTA, somewhat defeating the purpose of a lightweight baseline

Fundamental template-based limitations not addressed: templates don't guarantee actual synthesizability, ignore reaction conditions/stereochemistry/yield/cost; restricts exploration to biased subset of synthesizable space with no proposed solutions

Building block filtering technical issues: (1) MLP filter requires task-specific retraining, (2) precision-recall tradeoff where hard negative mining improves validation but hurts test performance suggesting overfitting, (3) NAM acknowledged as inadequate for non-additive properties

Experimental fairness concerns: (1) different PyTDC versions used than original PMO paper, (2) Valsartan SMARTS task removed because methods failed, (3) different template/building block catalogs across baselines confound comparisons, (4) some baselines evaluated on subsets only
Statistical rigor issues: some results with only 1 seed (SynthesisNet) or 3 seeds (f-RAG), large standard deviations in places, no significance testing reported

Missing critical analysis: limited interpretability of what GA learns, no diversity analysis of discovered molecules, no error analysis of failures, sensitivity to hyperparameters only explored on 2 PMO tasks, no experimental validation that discovered molecules are actually synthesizable

strengths: Well-motivated problem: Addresses genuine practical barrier of synthesis-agnostic models producing unsynthesizable molecules
Elegant genetic operator design: Custom operators (Grow, Shrink, Rerun, etc.) maintain validity by construction, cleaner than post-hoc projection
Guaranteed synthesizability: By design, all generated molecules have plausible synthesis routes
Comprehensive experimental evaluation: Extensive benchmarks across analog search, PMO (22 tasks), and docking with multiple baselines
Clear presentation: Well-written with informative figures and implementation details
Reproducibility effort: Ablations, hyperparameter details, and code availability promised
weaknesses: Limited novelty: GA + custom tree operators is incremental; building block filtering (MLP/NAM) is straightforward; SynGBO directly applies existing BO to SynGA. Synthesis trees explored by prior work (Gao et al. 2022b, 2024)
Efficiency claims not supported: SynGA is 3× slower than SynFormer (250m vs 80m), contradicting 'lightweight' positioning. Avoids projection model overhead but doesn't deliver computational gains

Empirical results don't justify approach: SynGA alone (13.366) significantly underperforms synthesis-agnostic methods on PMO (f-RAG 16.301, GPBO 16.304). Only SynGBO (16.426) approaches SOTA, requiring 100× inner-loop iterations and unclear total compute cost

Synthesis space limitations underexplored: Restricted to 91 templates, 5 steps max, 1000 Da cap. Doesn't guarantee synthesizability. Scalability to larger template sets acknowledged as problematic. Limited analysis of how constraints affect coverage

Building block filtering issues: Hard negative mining improves validation metrics (0.212→0.764 AUPRC) but degrades test performance (0.721→0.664 Morgan), indicating overfitting. NAM acknowledged as unable to capture complex properties; solution is coupling with stronger GP predictor, undermining elegance claim

Experimental quality concerns: PyTDC version mismatch (1.1.14 vs 0.3.6) affects PMO comparability; Valsartan SMARTS task removed for being 'difficult'; runtime comparisons use different hardware configurations. Limited ablations of individual operator contributions

Unclear positioning and practical guidance: Paper doesn't answer when practitioners should use SynGA vs alternatives, for which molecular problems it excels, or whether synthesis-agnostic + post-hoc synthesis checking is simpler. Missing analysis of discovery profiles, convergence, and molecular pattern coverage
Docking results limited: Only 3 receptors; SynGBO significantly outperforms SynGA, suggesting weak base algorithm for 3D. 3DSynthFlow achieves comparable results

Incomplete computational cost analysis: SynGBO's total compute overhead not transparently reported. Wall-clock comparisons unclear. Whether efficiency/quality trade-off justifies approach remains unanswered

Reproducibility gaps: Code/checkpoints available 'upon publication'. Some hyperparameter choices lack justification (kernel selection, ε-filtering = 0.1). Missing complexity analysis for Rerun operation scaling

strengths: Clear and well-motivated problem formulation with rigorous mathematical representation of synthesis routes as binary trees
Elegant custom genetic operators (Grow, Shrink, Rerun, Change) that enforce synthesizability by construction, avoiding expensive post-hoc projection
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple complementary tasks (analog search, 2D/3D property optimization, docking) with diverse baselines
Strong empirical results: guaranteed 100% valid routes, SynGBO achieves state-of-the-art or competitive performance on PMO and docking benchmarks
Impressive sample efficiency on docking tasks (better docking scores than most baselines with 1/4 oracle calls)
Practical advantages: lightweight, easily adaptable to new building blocks/templates, serves as modular component for future algorithms
Strong reproducibility efforts with extensive implementation details, promised code, hardware specs, and hyperparameter documentation
Well-structured presentation with clear mathematical formulation and helpful visual overview (Figure 1)
weaknesses: Limited core algorithmic novelty: applying GA to synthesis trees with standard mutation operations is relatively straightforward application of established concepts
Computational efficiency gap: SynGA is 3× slower than SynFormer on analog search (250m vs 80m), limiting practical deployment despite modularity arguments
Base SynGA underperforms synthesis-agnostic methods on PMO benchmark (13.366 vs 16.301 for f-RAG), requiring ML enhancement (SynGBO) for competitiveness
Building block filter shows inconsistency: strong validation metrics (AUROC 0.999) but worse performance on ChEMBL test set, with hard-negative mining hurting generalization
NAM limitations inadequately resolved: acknowledged poor performance on non-additive properties, solution is ad-hoc (ranking loss + GP coupling) without principled guidance
Fundamental template-based limitations: no guarantee of synthesizability, ignore reaction conditions/stereochemistry/yield/cost, biased subset of chemical space
Experimental concerns: removed Valsartan SMARTS task from PMO, different seed counts across baselines (f-RAG:3, SynthesisNet:1), PyTDC version dependencies affecting reproducibility
Runtime comparison limitations: different parallelization strategies and mixed CPU/GPU setups make fair comparison difficult
Limited ablations: Table 6 shows operator robustness but doesn't isolate individual operator contributions or analyze crossover effectiveness separately
Missing analysis of operator scalability: SMARTS caching acknowledged as not scaling to large libraries with no solutions proposed

strengths: Clear problem formulation and elegant technical contribution: Custom genetic operators (especially Rerun) for direct constraint embedding via synthesis trees are well-motivated and non-trivial, achieving 100% validity by construction

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: Three major problem settings (analog search, property optimization, docking) with comparisons to strong recent baselines, extensive ablations, and reproducibility details
Solid empirical results on sample-efficiency: SynGBO achieves competitive SOTA on PMO (16.426 AUC); docking results with 1/4 oracle calls of many baselines; perfect validity (100%)
Modular and practical design: Lightweight, ML-free SynGA can serve as standalone baseline or component in larger workflows; produces interpretable synthesis routes as output
Thorough documentation and reproducibility: Extensive appendices with implementation details, ablation studies, and promise of code release
weaknesses: Limited core novelty: Synthesis trees, template-based generation, and GA-based molecular design are well-established. Custom tree operators are straightforward engineering contributions lacking theoretical insight

Success heavily dependent on ML add-ons: Standalone SynGA significantly underperforms on PMO (13.366 vs 16.301 for synthesis-agnostic f-RAG); only SynGBO wrapper achieves SOTA. Block filtering critical for performance (Morgan: 0.459→0.721 on analog search), suggesting novelty lies in component combination rather than SynGA's core innovation

Inconsistent performance across tasks: Marginal improvements over SynFormer on analog search (0.711 vs 0.668 Morgan similarity) but 3× slower (250m vs 80m); underperforms on in-distribution datasets (DDS-10, ZINC); no clear guidance on when to prefer SynGA

Unfair and incomplete comparisons: Asymmetric comparison with synthesis-agnostic methods (larger search space); SynFormer uses 115 templates vs SynGA's 91 yet achieves similar/better performance; marginal improvements (0.125 AUC on PMO) within typical noise

Template-based fundamental limitations inadequately addressed: Acknowledged but unresolved constraints (no synthesizability guarantee, ignores conditions/stereochemistry/yield/cost); scalability concern noted as 'unlikely to scale to large libraries'; no analysis of chemical space lost to template constraints

Evaluation concerns and design choices lacking justification: Out-of-distribution issues on analog search (ChEMBL); hyperparameter ablations on only 2 PMO tasks; hard negative mining improves validation but hurts test performance (unexplained); ε-filtering approach (0.1) lacks principled justification; coupling NAM with GP appears ad-hoc

Limited insight into why the method works: No visualization/analysis of discovered molecules vs baselines; unclear why Rerun operation is effective; missing sensitivity analysis across template sets and block catalogs; questions about when practitioners should adopt SynGA remain unanswered

strengths: Well-engineered genetic operators (Grow, Shrink, Rerun, Change Internal/Leaf) that maintain syntactic validity by construction
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across analog search, property optimization, and docking with extensive appendices and ablations
Pragmatic ML enhancements through lightweight block filtering (classifier for analog search, NAM for property optimization)
Code availability and detailed reproducibility documentation support adoption and verification
Clear presentation of synthesis tree representation and unified framework for multiple molecular design tasks
weaknesses: Limited core novelty: operating GAs over synthesis routes is established in prior work (Gao et al. 2022b/2024); contributions feel incremental rather than introducing fundamentally new concepts

Mixed and inconsistent empirical results: raw SynGA significantly underperforms synthesis-agnostic baselines on PMO (13.366 vs 16.301 for f-RAG), contradicting the premise that synthesis constraints improve optimization; all competitive results require model-based augmentation (SynGBO), shifting advantage to the BO framework
Substantial runtime disadvantage: 3× slower than SynFormer (250m vs 80m for ChEMBL task) severely limits practical utility; at matched runtime (Table 8), SynGA underperforms (RR=0.175 vs 0.190)

Incomplete baseline comparisons: SynFormer comparison uses different training regimes (extensively trained for reconstruction vs. block relevance task only); different synthesis-aware baselines evaluated on different PMO subsets; Valsartan SMARTS task removed due to lack of signal, appearing to cherry-pick results

Fundamental limitations inadequately addressed: SMARTS implementation acknowledged as unscalable to large libraries; NAM correlations range from 0.877 to 0.647 showing poor performance on non-additive properties; proposed solution (coupling with GP) merely adds a stronger model rather than addressing the limitation

Unclear practical utility: paper does not establish when or why to use SynGA over alternatives; practitioners must choose between slower search (vs amortized methods), often inferior performance (vs synthesis-agnostic methods), or adding model-based components (negating lightweight GA advantage)

Methodological concerns: arbitrary design choices (ε=0.1 filtering parameter, mutation probability weights 0.125 vs 0.25) lack justification; Rerun operation's backtracking complexity and failure handling underexplored; crossover success rates not analyzed despite retry logic

Over-claimed contributions: synthesizability guarantee contradicted by acknowledgment that templates don't ensure actual synthesizability; GA contribution unclear as all competitive results come from model-based augmentation (SynGBO), not the algorithm itself

Limited analysis of method applicability: no clear guidance on when synthesis constraints help vs hurt optimization; synthesis-agnostic methods often outperform on standard benchmarks, suggesting constrained search can be limiting rather than beneficial

strengths: Elegant and principled design of custom genetic operators that enforce synthesizability by construction, avoiding pitfalls of post-hoc projection approaches
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple diverse tasks (analog search, 2D/3D property optimization) with extensive baselines and meaningful ablations
Strong empirical results achieving state-of-the-art on PMO benchmark (SynGBO 16.426) and excellent 3D docking performance with 1/4 oracle calls of baselines
Thoughtfully designed ML integration: fingerprint classifier for analog search and NAMs with pairwise ranking loss show complementary strengths when coupled with GPs
Lightweight ML-free baseline with promised code release makes work accessible and reproducible with detailed documentation and implementation details
Honest treatment of limitations with acknowledgment of template constraints and efficiency trade-offs; extensive appendices provide transparency
weaknesses: Computational efficiency gap: SynGA is 3× slower than SynFormer on analog search (250m vs 80m, Table 2), with limited analysis of efficiency-accuracy trade-offs for practical deployment
Limited fundamental algorithmic novelty: standard GA framework with task-specific operator engineering rather than conceptual advances; NAM application is straightforward

Synthesizability claims are overstated: templates don't guarantee synthesizability, don't account for reaction conditions/stereochemistry/yield/cost, and fixed template library restricts exploration to biased synthesis space

Evaluation methodology concerns: (1) search-based SynGA vs. trained models (SynFormer) is somewhat unfair; SynFormer outperforms on in-distribution sets (Table 9); (2) near-zero reconstruction rates suggest tasks may be insufficiently constrained; (3) PMO benchmark issues with Valsartan removal and PyTDC version incompatibilities

NAM limitations inadequately addressed: non-additive properties acknowledged but mitigation ad-hoc; Table 10 shows NAM+GP dominated by GP contribution, questioning NAM's role; α interpolation is simple knob with unclear generalization

Insufficient hyperparameter sensitivity analysis: mutation ablation (Table 6) on only 2 tasks with explicit caveat about generalization; population size, generations, and operator probabilities lack thorough exploration
Limited statistical rigor: no significance tests provided despite high variance in some results; with 4-5 seeds, some differences may not be statistically significant

Scope limitations: single-objective optimization only (real drug discovery is multi-objective); NSGA-II mentioned but not explored; no wet-lab validation or practitioner feedback on practical synthesizability
